title: Finally found the energy to finish Atom 118, which was designed +10 year ago
author: dderkomai
selftext:
I've been working on this mobile game for a few months (although the original concept dates back to 2015), and I believe it's now stable enough, so I've just launched it to gather some feedback. First, a game description:

>Atom 118 is a time-attack arcade game for iPhone and Android, inspired by games like Super Hexagon and One More Line. You drag protons, neutrons and electrons into an atom to build the next element, until you have built the whole periodic table. Every element you complete adds seconds to the clock, but if you rush, the atom collapses. There are radioactive elements that make your life harder, and power-ups that help you out.

Code was fully written by Codex fo the first weeks, and then I switched to Claude. I also used some DeepSeek for sub-agents implementing well defined tasks. I've been using OpenChamber as harness (which I find amazing) and Suno to create the original soundtrack. Godot is the game engine.

One of the things I've most happy about is how the music system turned out. In order to make the music adapt to your gameplay, the main track was split into several pieces, ranked by level of energy, and then classified into a finite state machine. I spent a lot of time listening for all possible transitions and their quality.

I'd love to hear what you think: is it too boring? Too hard maybe? Happy to send free links for the full game to anyone who wants to test further than the free demo: just comment here and I'll DM you one.

iPhone/iPad: [https://apps.apple.com/app/id6817310453](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6817310453)

Android: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.davidvilelafreire.atom118&referrer=utm\_source%3Dreddit-aigamedev%26utm\_campaign%3Dlaunch](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.davidvilelafreire.atom118&referrer=utm_source%3Dreddit-aigamedev%26utm_campaign%3Dlaunch)
